name: Linezolid
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder, slightly soluble in water.

The first oxazolidinone antibiotic; a WHO 'Reserve' (AWaRe) antibiotic and part of WHO-recommended regimens for drug-resistant tuberculosis. First approval/introduction: Discovered mid-1990s; US FDA 18 April 2000 (Pharmacia & Upjohn).

Binds the 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit, preventing formation of the 70S initiation complex; active against Gram-positive organisms including MRSA, VRE and penicillin-resistant pneumococci. Also a weak reversible MAO inhibitor. Receptor / target profile: Binds 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit and prevents formation of the 70S initiation complex; also a weak reversible non-selective MAO inhibitor.
Hepatic non-enzymatic oxidation of the morpholine ring (50–70%; CYP not involved)
Summary: Bioavailability ~100%; Tmax 1–2 h. ~31% protein bound. Non-enzymatic oxidation. Half-life 5–7 h.
Complicated skin and soft-tissue infections due to MRSA and other resistant Gram-positive bacteria
Nosocomial and community-acquired pneumonia caused by MRSA or resistant S. pneumoniae
MDR/XDR tuberculosis (as part of specialist regimens)
Adults: 600 mg every 12 h for 10–14 days (VRE: 14–28 days)
With or without food; avoid large amounts of tyramine-rich foods
Weekly CBC; monitor vision with courses >28 days
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use with or within 2 weeks of MAO inhibitors
Uncontrolled hypertension, phaeochromocytoma, thyrotoxicosis, carcinoid (unless monitored)
Concomitant serotonergic drugs, sympathomimetics, vasopressors (unless closely monitored)
Myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia, anaemia) – weekly CBC, especially >2 weeks
Peripheral and optic neuropathy with prolonged use (>28 days)
C. difficile diarrhoea; reserve for resistant Gram-positive infections
SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, triptans, tramadol (serotonin syndrome)
Avoid large amounts of tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, cured meats, soy sauce, tap beer, red wine).
Weekly CBC; visual acuity if >28 days; lactate if symptoms; glucose in diabetics.
ZEPHyR (Wunderink et al., Clin Infect Dis 2012) – higher clinical success than vancomycin in MRSA pneumonia.
Nix-TB (Conradie et al., NEJM 2020) – bedaquiline–pretomanid–linezolid achieved 90% favourable outcome in XDR/MDR-TB.
Report severe diarrhoea, rash or breathing difficulty
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
